record.ear: Fair and cold. High 27. Low 14. Ice at Whitestone thirteen inches; no cutting on the Sabbath.

lead.headline: Mr. Brandt to report tomorrow on the postcard and the 10:31 entry
lead.deck: Subpoena for Mr. Joseph Marchetti returnable at 10; Wilkes-Barre police find no Marchetti registered at any lodging house in the city
lead.body: Justice Thaddeus Rourke sits at 10 tomorrow on Mr. Walter Pruitt's petition, when Mr. Carl Brandt will report his comparison of the Wilkes-Barre postcard with the Riverhead ledger entry of 10:31 p.m. on November 6. The subpoena for Mr. Joseph Marchetti is returnable at the same hour. The Wilkes-Barre police informed Mr. Francis Gorman by wire on Friday that no person of that name is registered at any lodging house in the city. Mr. Gorman expects Mr. Marchetti 'or his reasons.'

columns.headline: Phonautograph Society's case for 1978 holds 1,040 records
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens reports 1,040 records received for 1978, its second copper case half full. Mr. Cyril Abbot asks that no further carols be sent after Thursday, the Society holding 212 of them, 'most of them the same one.'

columns.headline: Commission's order suspending the half-cent rise posted at utility offices
columns.body: The Public Service Commission's order suspending the proposed rate of 7 1/2 cents until it has heard the schedule, together with the Hum, on January 15 was posted yesterday at the Jamaica and Long Island City offices of Queens Light & Power. January bills will be rendered at 7 cents.

columns.headline: Christmas mail at the Flushing post office 40 per cent above last year
columns.body: The Flushing post office handled 188,000 pieces in the week, Postmaster Gilroy reports, 40 per cent above last December, of which 31,000 were parcels of the flat square shape of a record. He asks that records be packed in corrugated card and not in newspaper.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd's ships out of the pack at 4:50 a.m. into open water at 69 south. The whaler Larsen to part company.

speaker.ear: Fair and cold. High 27. Sunday: the ice men rest and the ice keeps working.

lead.headline: Court rings the lineman for ten tomorrow; Wilkes-Barre says no answer
lead.deck: The postcard and the ledger go head to head; the man who wrote one of them is on the line and off the map
lead.body: Tomorrow at ten Justice Rourke sits down with the handwriting man, the postcard from Wilkes-Barre and the ledger from Jamaica, and finds out whether the hand that wrote 'I fixed the instrument and went home' is the hand that wrote Riverhead at 10:31. The subpoena says Joseph Marchetti appears at the same hour. The Wilkes-Barre police say he is in no lodging house in their city. We have checked ours. He is not at the Speaker either.

columns.headline: Society's second box fills with carols, and 1978 asks for a change of tune
columns.body: Two hundred and twelve carols have gone into the Phonautograph Society's case for 1978, and Mr. Abbot says most of them are 'Silent Night,' sung by people who were not. No more after Thursday. In fifty years Queens will open the box and conclude we only knew one song.

columns.headline: Half-cent rise put on hold till the hum gets its hearing
columns.body: The Commission has suspended the utility's extra half cent until January 15, when it will hear the rate and the hum on the same afternoon. January bills come at seven cents. The company calls the suspension 'procedural.' So is a stay of execution.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'What do I get the exchange cat for Christmas?'
columns.body: Sir, Party Line has a saucer, a warm position and the respect of forty operators, which is more than most of us. She would accept a herring. Do not send it through the post; the Flushing office has troubles enough. Leave it with the supervisor and keep the line clear.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd is out of the pack and into open water. The whaler goes home. The ice stays.

record.ear: Cloudy and cold. High 30. Light snow tonight, an inch or less.

lead.headline: Some 3,000 walk the Whitestone ice field with receiving sets on Sunday
lead.deck: Police clear the field at 3:40 p.m. after a youth steps into a skinned-over cutting channel; Radio Division's man present, 'nothing received'
lead.body: About 3,000 persons walked onto the Bowery Bay Ice Company's Whitestone field yesterday afternoon, many carrying crystal sets and loop aerials, the watchman Mr. Daniel Rooney having reported WORS 1610 on the field's shanty receiver on the 9th. Police of the 109th Precinct cleared the field at 3:40 after a youth stepped into a cutting channel skinned with new ice and was pulled out by the crowd. Mr. Harold Pike of the Radio Division, present throughout, reported nothing received. The company has posted the field.

columns.headline: Mr. Brandt reports to Justice Rourke at 10 today; subpoena returnable
columns.body: Mr. Carl Brandt will report his comparison of the Wilkes-Barre postcard with the Riverhead ledger entry of 10:31 p.m. on November 6 at 10 this morning. The subpoena for Mr. Joseph Marchetti is returnable at the same hour. The Wilkes-Barre police have not found him.

columns.headline: Athletic Club five beat the Hoboken Turners 33 to 29 at the armory
columns.body: The Long Island City Athletic Club's basketball five beat the Hoboken Turners 33 to 29 at the armory on Saturday night before 1,100. Mr. Frank Dillon scored 14. No foul was disputed, and the armory's record was not called for.

columns.headline: Answering dolls to leave Newark by truck Wednesday for the Arcade
columns.body: The Newark maker of the answering doll has wired the Vantry Arcade's toy shop that 140 dolls will leave by motor truck on Wednesday night for delivery on Thursday the 20th. Each doll's six words are recorded at the works, the maker states, 'by the same lady.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd's ships in open water at 70 south, steaming for the Ross Barrier at seven knots.

speaker.ear: Grey, and snow tonight. High 30. Snow is the only thing in Queens that falls quietly.

lead.headline: Same hand on the card and the ledger, and the hand stays in Pennsylvania
lead.deck: Brandt says Marchetti wrote Riverhead at 10:31; Marchetti says nothing, from wherever he is; the judge issues a bench warrant and a sigh
lead.body: The handwriting man stood up at ten past ten and said the man who wrote 'I fixed the instrument and went home' also wrote the Riverhead entry at 10:31, 'to a degree I would put in writing.' Joseph Marchetti did not come. His name was called three times. Justice Rourke issued a bench warrant, which is a letter you cannot refuse, if you are there to receive it. Walter Pruitt is clear of the 10:31. Nobody yet knows what a lineman wanted with Riverhead.

columns.headline: Three thousand walk the ice for WORS and get a cold reception
columns.body: Three thousand people walked out on the Whitestone ice with crystal sets on Sunday to hear WORS 1610, and heard each other. A boy went through a cutting channel and was hauled out by a chain of strangers. The police cleared the field. The ice men would like it back.

columns.headline: Club five puts Hoboken on hold, 33 to 29
columns.body: The Athletic Club five beat the Hoboken Turners at the armory on Saturday, and for once nobody asked to hear the record. Frank Dillon scored fourteen and thanked the referee, which is a first in that building. Eleven hundred went home happy and hoarse.

columns.headline: Answering dolls on the road from Newark, every one in the same lady's voice
columns.body: A hundred and forty answering dolls leave Newark Wednesday by truck. The maker says all six words on every doll were recorded by one lady at the works. That is 840 words for one lady, and not one of them is 'no.' The Arcade expects them Thursday morning.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd is steaming for the Barrier at seven knots in open water. No pack, no whaler, no excuses.

record.ear: Snow ended, one inch. Clearing. High 29. Low 18.

lead.headline: Mr. Brandt finds the 10:31 entry and the Wilkes-Barre postcard in one hand
lead.deck: Mr. Marchetti fails to appear on subpoena; Justice Rourke issues a bench warrant and reserves decision on Mr. Pruitt's petition until January 7
lead.body: Mr. Carl Brandt told Justice Rourke at 10:12 yesterday that the Riverhead ledger entry of 10:31 p.m. on November 6 and the postcard signed 'J. Marchetti' are 'in one hand, to a degree I would put in writing.' Mr. Joseph Marchetti was called three times and did not appear. The Justice issued a bench warrant and reserved decision until January 7. Mr. Gorman asked that Mr. Pruitt's name be cleared of the 10:31 entry. The Justice said that 'the ledger has cleared it already.'

columns.headline: Board of Elections to receive the Riverhead returns afresh on January 3
columns.body: Chairman Delaney announced at 4 p.m. yesterday that the Board will receive the Riverhead returns afresh from the Suffolk clerk on January 3, once by wire and once by paper, in the presence of counsel. Mr. Hoover's majority is not affected, the Chairman said.

columns.headline: Interborough fits 26 of 40 Astoria trains with contact shoe heaters
columns.body: The Interborough reports 26 of its 40 Astoria line trains fitted with contact shoe heaters, the remainder promised by the 31st. Delays on the Queensboro Plaza curve from ice on the third rail fell to four on Sunday night from nineteen a week before.

columns.headline: Hanrahan fund closes at 1,118 dollars; Father Leahy named trustee
columns.body: The Bowery Bay Ice Company closed the Hanrahan family fund last night at 1,118 dollars, received at its College Point office and the Record's counter. Father Leahy of St. Fidelis is trustee. Mrs. Hanrahan has asked the Record to thank 'every man on the Sound.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Justice Rourke's bench warrant was wired to the Wilkes-Barre police at 3:30 p.m.

columns.headline: Restwell Mattress Company reports sales tripled since November
columns.body: The Restwell Mattress Company states that it sold 1,140 mattresses in the four weeks since Professor Tobias Lull began his evening instruction over WLIC, against 380 in the same weeks last year. The company attributes the increase to the season. It will add a second shift at its Borden Avenue works.

columns.headline: A retired teacher writes on the spelling of next October's event
columns.body: A correspondent of Long Island City, for thirty-one years a teacher, writes to observe that the Bureau's bulletin of last week gives three spellings of the same name in nine lines. She does not offer a fourth. She asks only that the Bureau select one, and has returned the bulletin, marked.

columns.headline: Six-day men at the Garden ask that the radios be turned down
columns.body: Riders in the six-day race at Madison Square Garden complained through their managers last night that receiving sets in the upper tiers were tuned to a Queens station at ten o'clock, and that two men on the track had begun to count. The management has asked patrons to use earphones.

columns.headline: Wanted: second-hand receiving set, must get WLIC clear
columns.body: Wife has not slept since September and has now heard about it from her sister. Will pay fair price for any set, crystal or valve, that gets WLIC clear at ten o'clock. Tel. Stillwell 3381 evenings before ten only.

back.foot: The Borough Record. Printed at Long Island City.

speaker.ear: Clearing, and an inch of snow to show for it. High 29.

lead.headline: Board will hear Riverhead again, once in each ear
lead.deck: Wire on the left, paper on the right, January 3; Pruitt cleared, Marchetti wanted, Hoover still President
lead.body: The Board of Elections, having lost a lineman and found a postcard, will start Riverhead over. On January 3 the Suffolk clerk will send the returns once by wire and once by paper, and counsel will sit and listen to both. Chairman Delaney says Mr. Hoover's majority is not affected, which he has said so often the Board could record it and save his voice. Walter Pruitt went home cleared last night. Joseph Marchetti did not go home at all, or not to Corona.

columns.headline: Shoe heaters on 26 trains, and the Plaza curve stops giving the cold shoulder
columns.body: Twenty-six Astoria trains now carry contact shoe heaters, and the Plaza curve had four ice delays on Sunday against nineteen the Sunday before. The other fourteen trains by New Year's Eve, the Interborough says. Guards report the third rail now 'sizzles politely.'

columns.headline: Judge sends a warrant down the line to Wilkes-Barre
columns.body: Justice Rourke's bench warrant for Joseph Marchetti went to the Wilkes-Barre police by wire at half past three. The police there have looked in every lodging house. They will now try the others. Mr. Marchetti, if you are reading the Speaker, the judge only wants a word.

columns.headline: The Sound rings true: Hanrahan fund closes at 1,118 dollars
columns.body: The fund for Michael Hanrahan's widow and children closed at 1,118 dollars last night, given by ice men, coal men, Record readers and Speaker readers, who are mostly the same people on different days. Father Leahy holds it. Mrs. Hanrahan says thank you to every man on the Sound.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd reports fog at 72 south and penguins on the wire. He says penguins. We say static.

record.ear: Fair and colder. High 24. Low 11 tonight. Wind northwest, fresh.

lead.headline: Arcade counter limits valves to two sleeves a customer at 1 dollar 04
lead.deck: Newark works to close for Christmas week from Saturday; hardware men in Jamaica and Flushing report the same limit; eggs 66, coal 15
lead.body: The Vantry Arcade's hardware counter yesterday limited customers to two six-sleeves of receiving valves at 1 dollar 04 the sleeve, up four cents in nine days, its stock then standing at 38 sleeves. The Newark works, which supplies most of the borough, closes for Christmas week from Saturday. The counterman attributes the demand to crystal sets 'outgrown by Christmas morning.' Hardware men in Jamaica and Flushing report the same limit. Eggs are 66 cents the dozen at Dutch Kills market. Coal holds at 15 dollars.

columns.headline: Phonautograph Society to close its carol list at 236
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens will accept no more carols for its 1978 case after tomorrow, having received 236. Mr. Cyril Abbot said 141 were 'Silent Night.' Records on other subjects remain welcome until March 1 at the Jamaica office.

columns.headline: Mr. Lucius Pell files a brief of 61 pages against the Listening Act
columns.body: Mr. Lucius Pell, counsel to the Queens Real Estate Owners' Association, filed a brief of 61 pages with the Senate Judiciary Committee yesterday opposing the Listening Act. Its first section argues that a building recorded before 1929 'cannot be licensed retrospectively without consenting.' The hearing is January 9.

columns.headline: Bowery Bay company fences its Whitestone field; shanty set removed
columns.body: The Bowery Bay Ice Company put up 400 yards of snow fence along the Whitestone shore yesterday and removed the receiving set from its field shanty. Mr. Owen Pratt, foreman, said the set 'was for the weather' and the men could do without it. Cutting resumed at 7.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Wilkes-Barre police report a Joseph Marchetti in the 1920 city directory. The address is a vacant lot.

speaker.ear: Fair and colder. High 24. Wind from the northwest and a draught from Newark.

lead.headline: Valve men put the borough on a ration: two sleeves and hold the line
lead.deck: Newark shuts for Christmas, the sleeve hits a dollar and four, and every father in Queens is buying spares for a set he hasn't wrapped yet
lead.body: The Arcade counterman has started rationing valves, two sleeves to a customer, and the queue at his counter yesterday went out the door and past the luncheonette. The Newark works closes Saturday for Christmas week, and nobody in Queens wants to be the house that goes quiet on the 25th. The price is a dollar and four cents. Eggs are sixty-six. Your crystal set does not need valves, sir. Your crystal set is not what you are buying for.

columns.headline: Society calls time on 'Silent Night', the quietest thing in the box
columns.body: Of 236 carols sent to the Phonautograph Society for 1978, 141 are 'Silent Night,' and Mr. Abbot is closing the list tomorrow. Send him your ordinary Tuesdays instead. The future, he says, already knows how Christmas goes. It does not know how Tuesday goes.

columns.headline: Landlords' counsel argues an old wall is off the record
columns.body: Mr. Lucius Pell has sent Albany 61 pages saying a building that was listening before 1929 cannot be licensed without its consent. We asked a building. It said nothing, but it heard us ask. The hearing is January 9. Bring a coat; Albany is colder than Mr. Pell.

columns.headline: Ice men take the set off the ice and leave WORS out in the cold
columns.body: Bowery Bay has fenced its Whitestone field and taken the radio out of the shanty, the foreman saying it was 'for the weather.' The weather will now be found out by looking. Three thousand people with crystal sets are asked to do their listening from shore.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Wilkes-Barre has found Marchetti's address in the 1920 directory. It is a vacant lot. Nobody answered.

record.ear: Fair and cold. High 26. Low 13. Fourteen inches at Whitestone.

lead.headline: Ice cutter married at College Point under an arch of 24 saws
lead.deck: Mr. Thomas Garvey and Miss Agnes Dowd wed at 4 p.m.; Whitestone field stops for the hour; ceremony record played twice at the breakfast
lead.body: Mr. Thomas Garvey, 27, an ice cutter of the Bowery Bay Ice Company, and Miss Agnes Dowd, 22, of 14th Avenue, were married at 4 p.m. yesterday at the First Methodist Church of College Point by the Rev. Albert Sayre. Twenty-four men of the Whitestone field formed an arch of ice saws at the church door. The company stopped cutting for the hour. The ceremony was recorded at the bride's mother's request and played twice at the breakfast, the second time at the groom's.

columns.headline: Answering dolls due at the Arcade this morning; 140 orders to be filled
columns.body: The Newark truck carrying 140 answering dolls is expected at the Vantry Arcade by 8 this morning, the toy shop's proprietress says. Orders will be filled in the order taken. She asks customers not to press the dolls' hands in the queue.

columns.headline: Boulder Canyon bill to the President; Phonautograph Society wires Washington
columns.body: The Boulder Canyon Project bill, passed by the House on Tuesday, is expected to be signed by President Coolidge this week. The Phonautograph Society of Queens wired the Interior Department last night asking leave to record the Colorado River at the site 'before and after.'

columns.headline: Valves: 22 sleeves left at the Arcade counter; limit holds at two
columns.body: The Arcade hardware counter had 22 six-sleeves of receiving valves at closing last night against 38 on Tuesday morning. The limit of two a customer holds, and the price at 1 dollar 04. A Flushing counter reports none left.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd's ships at 74 south in open sea. The Barrier is expected within the week.

speaker.ear: Fair and cold. High 26. Fourteen inches of ice, and the dolls are in town.

lead.headline: The answering doll arrives, and three of them talk back too much
lead.deck: A hundred and forty little ladies from Newark, six words apiece; the toy shop sends three home for saying seven
lead.body: The Newark truck got to the Arcade at twenty past eight with a hundred and forty answering dolls, and the toy-shop lady played every one before she let it out the door. Three said seven words. The order says six. She put those three back in their box and sent them to Newark on the afternoon truck, and she will not tell us the seventh word, though we asked twice. The other hundred and thirty-seven are on their way to Christmas trees, holding their tongues.

columns.headline: Ice cutter weds under twenty-four saws, and the bride cuts in
columns.body: Thomas Garvey of the Whitestone field married Agnes Dowd under an arch of ice saws, the most frightening thing a bride has walked under since the elevated. The service was recorded and played twice at the breakfast. The second time the groom wept. The first time he was listening.

columns.headline: The Society wants the Colorado on the record before Washington cuts it off
columns.body: The Boulder Dam bill is on the President's desk, and the Phonautograph Society has wired Washington to record the river before and after. Mr. Abbot says no river has been recorded before it stopped. We say the Colorado will not stop. It will just be put on hold.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Not on the ice, now the ice men have pulled the plug
columns.body: Since Bowery Bay carried the receiving set out of its Whitestone shanty, nobody has reported WORS 1610 from the Sound. This proves nothing, says our correspondent, except that you cannot hear a station without a set. Readers with sets: keep listening, and write in.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd is at seventy-four south and no pack in sight. The Barrier is somewhere ahead, keeping quiet.

record.ear: Cloudy and milder. High 34. Rain or snow tomorrow night.

lead.headline: Arcade sells 137 answering dolls by noon; three returned to Newark
lead.deck: Truck arrives 8:20 a.m. with 96 waiting; each record played before sale; three 'said seven words where the order says six'
lead.body: The Newark truck reached the Vantry Arcade at 8:20 a.m. yesterday with 140 answering dolls, 96 persons then waiting at the toy and stationery shop. The proprietress played each doll's record before sale. Three, she said, 'said seven words where the order says six,' and were returned to Newark on the 2 p.m. truck. She declined to give the seventh word. The remaining 137 were sold by 11:50.

columns.headline: President to sign Boulder Canyon bill today; Queens engineers to debate the dam
columns.body: President Coolidge is expected to sign the Boulder Canyon Project bill today. The Queens Society of Engineers will debate at 8 tonight at the Flushing Y.M.C.A. 'whether a dam of 700 feet will be audible,' on the motion of Mr. Gustav Ernst of Astoria.

columns.headline: Christmas trees 1 dollar 50 to 4 dollars at Queensboro Plaza
columns.body: The Vermont growers selling under the elevated at Queensboro Plaza report 1,900 trees sold since Saturday at 1 dollar 50 to 4 dollars. Mr. Elias Fenn of Bennington says Queens buyers 'tap the trunk and listen,' which is not done in Vermont.

columns.headline: Weather Bureau gives Christmas Eve 'snow probable'; mild until Sunday
columns.body: The Weather Bureau's holiday forecast, issued at 4 p.m. yesterday, gives milder weather until Sunday, rain or snow tomorrow night, and 'snow probable' on Monday, Christmas Eve, with a high of 28. The ice companies fear for the Whitestone field.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Wilkes-Barre police report no trace of Mr. Joseph Marchetti. The bench warrant remains outstanding.

speaker.ear: Milder and cloudy. High 34. The ice men are watching the thermometer like a ball game.

lead.headline: Coolidge signs the big dam, and Astoria asks if it will hum along
lead.deck: Seven hundred feet of concrete across the Colorado; the engineers meet tonight to argue whether you will hear it from Queens
lead.body: President Coolidge signed the Boulder Dam bill today with a pen and without a speech, which is how he does most things. The dam will be seven hundred feet high, the biggest wall ever built, and in Queens a wall is a thing that listens. Mr. Gustav Ernst of Astoria will ask the engineers tonight at the Flushing Y whether a dam that size will be audible. He has already measured the hum at forty-one cycles. He would like the dam to pick a different note.

columns.headline: Vermont tree men say Queens has a funny ring to it
columns.body: The tree men from Bennington have sold 1,900 trees under the Plaza at a dollar fifty and up. In Vermont you shake a tree to see the needles hold. In Queens you knock on it and put your ear to the bark. Nobody has said what for.

columns.headline: The Listening Lady: who wanted the dolls with the extra word?
columns.body: Nobody got them, darlings. But the lady at the front of Thursday's queue, in the good fox collar, asked twice what the seventh word was, and was heard at the luncheonette to say she had 'a fair idea.' So have we. Neither of us is saying.

columns.headline: Marchetti's trail turns to dead air in Wilkes-Barre
columns.body: The Wilkes-Barre police have looked everywhere a lineman might sleep and found no Joseph Marchetti. The warrant stays out. Somewhere in Pennsylvania a man with a valise and a receiving set is keeping his volume down, and the judge would like a word before New Year's.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The engineers meet tonight on the dam. Forty-one cycles has been invited. It has not replied.

record.ear: Rain turning to snow tonight. High 36. Whitestone field idle in the thaw.

lead.headline: Boulder Canyon Act signed; Queens engineers vote 41 to 38 a dam can be heard
lead.deck: Society of Engineers sits until 11:05 p.m. on Mr. Gustav Ernst's motion; utility's engineer abstains, 'the matter being before the Commission'
lead.body: President Coolidge signed the Boulder Canyon Project Act yesterday, providing for a dam of about 700 feet on the Colorado. At the Flushing Y.M.C.A. last night the Queens Society of Engineers debated on Mr. Gustav Ernst's motion that 'a wall of that mass, once loaded, will be heard at a distance.' The motion carried 41 to 38. Mr. Ernst's figure of 41 cycles for the Hum was read into the minutes. The engineer of Queens Light & Power abstained, 'the matter being before the Commission.'

columns.headline: Week's count: 1,412 calls to the exchange for the hour of a Christmas service
columns.body: The Queens exchange reports 1,412 calls in the week to last night asking the hour of a Christmas service, against 960 a year ago. The supervisor has posted a list of 61 churches at every position. Party Line, the exchange cat, has been moved to position 43.

columns.headline: Newark to send three replacement answering dolls by Monday
columns.body: The Newark maker of the answering doll wired the Vantry Arcade's toy shop yesterday that three replacement dolls will be delivered on Monday morning, recorded again 'by the same lady, on a fresh morning.' The three returned dolls are 'under examination.'

columns.headline: St. Rita's pageant at 4 tomorrow; parish hall seats 300
columns.body: The St. Rita's parish Christmas pageant will be given at 4 p.m. tomorrow in the parish hall, Long Island City, by 62 children, with Sister Bernadette at the organ. The performance will be recorded and the record played after the eleven o'clock Mass on Christmas Day.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd's ships within 200 miles of the Barrier at 5 a.m. The expedition will keep Christmas at sea.

speaker.ear: Rain, then snow. High 36. The Sound is sulking and the ice men are sulking with it.

lead.headline: Engineers vote 41 to 38 that a dam can be heard, and 41 sounds familiar
lead.deck: Three hours at the Flushing Y on whether concrete talks; the utility's man abstains, as is his custom with noises
lead.body: The Queens Society of Engineers sat until five past eleven last night and voted, forty-one to thirty-eight, that a dam seven hundred feet high on the Colorado will be audible at a distance once it fills. Nobody said what distance. Mr. Ernst of Astoria, who carried it, read his forty-one cycles into the minutes, and the meeting noticed the count was the same. The man from Queens Light & Power abstained. He abstains from all noises. The President signed the dam at lunch.

columns.headline: A record week at the exchange: 1,412 people ring to ask when midnight is
columns.body: Fourteen hundred and twelve callers this week asked the operators what time Midnight Mass begins. The answer, the operators wish to say, is midnight. Some churches start at a quarter to, out of nerves, so the list is pinned up. Party Line has moved over a seat for it.

columns.headline: Newark recalls three dolls for talking out of turn
columns.body: The three answering dolls who said seven words are 'under examination' in Newark, and three replacements arrive at the Arcade on Monday, recorded on a fresh morning by the same lady. We hope she slept well. Six words, madam. Count them out loud.

columns.headline: St. Rita's shepherds go on tomorrow at four, and the playback is Christmas
columns.body: Sixty-two children of St. Rita's give the pageant tomorrow at four in the parish hall, and the record will be played after the eleven o'clock on Christmas Day, so the shepherds may hear themselves at last. The second shepherd has his lines. The ox has asked for more.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd will keep Christmas at sea, 200 miles from the Barrier. He has a gramophone. Of course he does.

editorial.headline: No stocking for Lilith this Christmas
editorial.body: Commissioner of Public Morals Horace Pell, the man who closed eleven dance halls this year to protect the virtue of the working girl, woke on Thursday to find his own socks, his own garters and his own name hung from the flagpole of Borough Hall, beside the deed to the Starlight Ballroom on Steinway Street, which he has owned through his brother-in-law since 1925 and which, alone among dance halls, was never once raided. A lipstick spider decorated the deed. The Commissioner says it is a forgery. The deed is on file. We wish our readers a merry Christmas and remind them that a man may own a ballroom and still disapprove of dancing. It is called character.

record.ear: Snow, two inches, ending this morning. High 30. Colder tonight.

lead.headline: Thaw halts the Sound ice harvest at 26,800 tons; fields closed until frost
lead.deck: Rain on the Whitestone field Friday night softens the ice to eleven inches; Bowery Bay company lays off 210 men with half a week's pay
lead.body: The three ice companies on the Sound stopped cutting at noon yesterday, the rain of Friday night having left water standing on the Whitestone and Willets Point fields and the ice softened to eleven inches. The harvest stands at 26,800 tons housed since November 24. The Bowery Bay Ice Company has laid off 210 men until hard frost returns, with half a week's pay for Christmas. Mr. Owen Pratt, foreman, said the field 'will freeze again by the New Year or not at all.'

columns.headline: St. Rita's pageant at 4 today; parents asked not to record from the seats
columns.body: The St. Rita's Christmas pageant will be given by 62 children at 4 p.m. today in the parish hall. Sister Bernadette asks that parents not record from the seats, the hall's own system being 'sufficient and better placed.' Admission is free; the collection is for the coal fund.

columns.headline: Phonautograph Society's second case passes 1,300 records; third ordered
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens received its 1,300th record for 1978 on Friday, a ten-minute account by a Maspeth grocer of his shop on an ordinary Thursday. Mr. Cyril Abbot said the second copper case is three-quarters full and a third has been ordered.

columns.headline: Astoria Hum petitioners name four witnesses for January 15
columns.body: The Astoria petitioners on the Hum will be represented before the Public Service Commission on January 15 by Alderman Feeney and four witnesses, among them Mr. Gustav Ernst and the Ditmars Avenue baker Mr. Hesse, who will bring his cellar record of 1913.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: The Arcade hardware counter had nine six-sleeves of valves at closing. The limit is now one a customer.

speaker.ear: Two inches of snow, then colder. High 30. Christmas is two days off and so is the ice.

lead.headline: Valves run low and Queens faces a silent night it didn't ask for
lead.deck: Nine sleeves left at the Arcade, one to a customer, Newark shut till New Year; the pawnshops are buying valves back
lead.body: The Arcade counterman had nine sleeves of valves at closing last night and has cut the limit to one a customer. Newark is shut until the New Year. Jamaica is out. Flushing is out. A pawnbroker on Jackson Avenue is buying used valves at twelve cents apiece and selling them at twenty-five, which is either good business or a sin, and it is Christmas, so it is both. Mind your set this week. Do not kick it. Do not let your uncle fix it.

columns.headline: Thaw cuts the ice men off mid-sentence
columns.body: Rain on the Sound stopped the harvest at noon yesterday with 26,800 tons in the houses and the fields standing in water. Bowery Bay sent 210 men home. Mr. Pratt says the field will freeze again by New Year's or not at all, which covers it.

columns.headline: Sister Bernadette pulls rank on the parents: the hall has the better reception
columns.body: St. Rita's pageant is at four today, and Sister Bernadette has asked parents not to bring their own machines, the hall's system being 'sufficient and better placed.' It is also not standing on a chair in a good hat. The collection is for the coal fund.

columns.headline: The hum gets a four-man band for January 15
columns.body: Alderman Feeney will take four witnesses to the Commission on January 15, among them Mr. Ernst with his forty-one cycles and Mr. Hesse the baker with his cellar from 1913. The company will bring its engineer, who abstains. A four-man band against a man who does not play.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd's flagship reports carols on the ship's gramophone and the dogs singing along. The dogs are flat.

record.ear: Snow probable this evening. High 28. Low 19. Ice fields closed.

lead.headline: St. Rita's pageant given before 340; second shepherd's lines complete
lead.deck: Sixty-two children in the parish hall at 4 p.m.; the record to be played after the eleven o'clock Mass tomorrow; collection of 61 dollars to the coal fund
lead.body: The St. Rita's Christmas pageant was given at 4 p.m. yesterday in the parish hall before 340 persons. Sixty-two children performed. The second shepherd spoke his lines complete. The ox, played by two boys of the sixth grade, was 'heard but not seen at the manger,' Sister Bernadette said, having become separated at the rear. The organ amens were four, as written. The hall's record will be played after the eleven o'clock Mass tomorrow. The collection, 61 dollars, goes to the coal fund.

columns.headline: Athletic Club five lose at Paterson 30 to 27 in an extra period
columns.body: The Long Island City Athletic Club five lost to the Paterson Crescents 30 to 27 in an extra period at Paterson on Saturday night, Mr. Frank Dillon scoring eleven. The club protested a foul. The Paterson hall has no house system, and the protest was dismissed.

columns.headline: Arcade shops open until 10 tonight; replacement dolls expected at 8
columns.body: The Vantry Arcade's eleven shops remain open until 10 tonight and close tomorrow. Three replacement answering dolls are expected from Newark at 8 this morning for the toy shop's last three customers, who have been notified by the exchange.

columns.headline: Exchange to carry Christmas calls with 12 extra operators until 2 a.m.
columns.body: The Queens exchange will have 12 extra operators on duty from 6 tonight until 2 a.m. for Christmas calls, the supervisor reports. Calls to Pennsylvania and Ohio are expected to wait up to forty minutes. Callers are asked not to ring the exchange about the wait.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: The Arcade hardware counter sold its last valve at 6:10 p.m. Saturday. Newark's first delivery is expected January 2.

speaker.ear: Snow tonight, they say, and we believe them for once. High 28.

lead.headline: The ox gets lost on the way to the manger, and St. Rita's plays it by ear
lead.deck: The second shepherd is word perfect, the angels hold the note, and the back half of the ox wanders off into the cloakroom
lead.body: Three hundred and forty people saw the St. Rita's pageant yesterday, and every one of them will tell you about the ox. The ox was two boys from the sixth grade, and halfway through the second act the front of the ox arrived at the manger without the back. The back was heard but not seen, in the cloakroom, mooing to the end. The second shepherd was word perfect. Sister Bernadette counted four amens, as written. The record plays after the eleven o'clock tomorrow. Bring the boys.

columns.headline: Club five loses at Paterson, where nobody kept the record
columns.body: The Athletic Club five went to Paterson on Saturday and lost 30 to 27 in overtime on a foul nobody can prove, the Paterson hall having no house system. The club protested. Paterson said prove it. That is what comes of playing in New Jersey.

columns.headline: Newark's replacement dolls arrive and count to six on the line
columns.body: Three fresh answering dolls reached the Arcade at five past eight, and the toy-shop lady played each one twice. Six words apiece. Three customers went home happy. She still will not tell us the seventh word, and has stopped answering the question.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Can I ring Santa Claus?'
columns.body: Little girl, the North Pole has no exchange, but the operator on position 9 has a deep voice and a great deal of patience, and from six tonight she will take your order. Speak slowly. Stay on the line. Do not ask her about the dolls.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Valves are gone from the Arcade till January 2. If your set dies tonight, sing.

record.ear: Snow, three inches, ending at dawn. High 27. Merry Christmas to our readers.

lead.headline: Carols at St. Fidelis, College Point, as recorded on Christmas Eve
lead.deck: The parish record of the 7 p.m. carol service, transcribed by the Record; 410 present; the Hanrahan family in the third pew
lead.body: 7:02 p.m. Organ. 7:04, 'O Come, All Ye Faithful,' four verses, congregation; a child's voice ahead of the organ in the second verse. 7:09, 'It Came Upon the Midnight Clear,' choir. 7:14, Father Leahy reads from St. Luke. 7:21, 'Silent Night,' the ice cutters of the Bowery Bay company, unaccompanied, the third verse in German. 7:25, a pause of eleven seconds. 7:26, 'Hark! the Herald Angels Sing,' all. 7:31, the blessing. 7:33, the doors.

columns.headline: Christmas Eve snow, three inches; exchange carries 401,000 calls
columns.body: Snow began at 6:40 p.m. and three inches had fallen by 2 a.m. The Queens exchange carried 401,000 calls between 6 p.m. and 2 a.m., the most in its history, the supervisor reports, with a longest wait, to Pittsburgh, of 52 minutes.

columns.headline: Byrd's expedition keeps Christmas at sea near the Barrier
columns.body: Commander Byrd's Christmas message, heard by the Navy at Bay Shore at 1:50 a.m., states that the City of New York kept Christmas at sea with a service at 8 a.m., a gramophone and 'a dinner chiefly of seal.' He sends greetings to the boroughs.

columns.headline: Coal yards closed today; Dutchman stops at all eleven houses of 1925
columns.body: The borough's coal yards are closed today, the Vernon Avenue yard having delivered until 9 last night with every horse out. Mr. Anton Keller reports that the Percheron Dutchman stopped at all eleven houses of his 1925 round, the two vacant ones included.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: No Record will be sold from the kerb boxes before 7 this morning. The carriers are at Mass.

speaker.ear: Three inches of snow on Christmas morning. High 27. Merry Christmas from the cheap seats.

lead.headline: Silent night, thin walls: Christmas Eve as heard next door
lead.deck: The Record printed a church; we print the flat next to the night editor's, by kind permission of nobody
lead.body: Seven o'clock: a piano, one finger, 'Jingle Bells.' Seven twenty: a man asks where the scissors are. A woman says where they always are. Eight: a child is told he may open one. He opens the big one. Nine: an uncle sings 'Adeste' in Latin he made up. Ten: a long argument about a turkey. Eleven forty: the whole flat goes out to Mass, and the hum keeps the rooms company. Two: they come home quietly, and somebody says, to nobody, 'That was a good one.'

columns.headline: The exchange is engaged all night: 401,000 calls on Christmas Eve
columns.body: Four hundred and one thousand calls went through the Queens exchange between six and two, a record, and every operator heard every family she connected say the same four things in a different order. Pittsburgh was fifty-two minutes. Party Line slept through it on position 43.

columns.headline: Dutchman calls on his old customers, even the ones who moved out of range
columns.body: Dutchman the Percheron pulled coal until nine and stopped at all eleven houses on his 1925 round, including the two whose customers moved in 1926. Mr. Keller let him stand at each for a minute. Dutchman went on. It is Christmas, and a horse may keep his own counsel.

columns.headline: Byrd keeps Christmas on seal and a gramophone, and the penguins tune in
columns.body: Commander Byrd's men kept Christmas at sea with a service, a gramophone and a dinner, he says, chiefly of seal. We hope it was a big seal. The message reached Bay Shore at ten to two. The dogs send no greeting. They had the seal's leftovers.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The St. Rita's record plays after the eleven o'clock today. The back half of the ox has been found.

record.ear: Fair and cold. High 24. Low 12. The Sound refreezing.

lead.headline: WORS 1610 heard on Christmas night playing a carol no organist can name
lead.deck: Thirty-one reports from Astoria, Woodside and Jackson Heights between 9:40 and 9:52 p.m.; two households record it; St. Rita's and St. Fidelis organists fail to identify the tune
lead.body: The Queens exchange logged 31 reports between 9:40 and 9:52 p.m. on Christmas night of a station announcing itself as WORS 1610 and playing a carol for organ and voices. Two households in Woodside recorded it. The records were played at 11 last night at the Phonautograph Society's Jamaica office to Sister Bernadette of St. Rita's, and the organist of St. Fidelis, neither of whom could name the tune or find its words in any hymnal held. Mr. Harold Pike of the Radio Division received nothing.

columns.headline: St. Rita's pageant record played after the eleven o'clock; about 200 hear it
columns.body: The St. Rita's pageant record was played in the parish hall after the eleven o'clock Mass yesterday to about 200. Sister Bernadette reports that the ox's separation, being audible in the record as two voices in two rooms, 'was received well.'

columns.headline: Christmas Eve burglary in Jackson Heights; parlour record given to police
columns.body: The house of Mr. Leonard Hale, 81st Street, Jackson Heights, was entered about midnight on Christmas Eve while the family was at Midnight Mass. Silver and a fur coat worth 400 dollars were taken. Mr. Hale has given the police the parlour system's record of those hours.

columns.headline: No valves in stock borough-wide; Newark's first delivery January 2
columns.body: Hardware men in Jamaica, Flushing, Astoria and the Vantry Arcade report no receiving valves in stock. The Newark works reopens on the 2nd. A Jackson Avenue pawnbroker reports buying 300 used valves since Saturday at 12 cents. Eggs are 68 cents.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd's ships at the Barrier edge at 6 a.m. Eastern time. The Commander seeks a harbour to the east.

speaker.ear: Cold again. High 24. The Sound is freezing back up, like an uncle after Christmas.

lead.headline: WORS rings in Christmas with a carol nobody has ever heard of
lead.deck: Thirty-one homes catch it at twenty to ten; two record it; Sister Bernadette listens twice and says it is not in the book
lead.body: At twenty to ten on Christmas night WORS 1610 came up in thirty-one parlours from Astoria to Jackson Heights with an organ, a choir and a carol, and nobody knew the tune. Two families in Woodside got it on the record. Last night the Phonautograph Society played it to Sister Bernadette and the St. Fidelis organist. Sister Bernadette listened twice and said it was 'a carol, certainly, and not one of ours.' Mr. Pike of the Radio Division heard nothing, which is his carol.

columns.headline: Burglar breaks in on Christmas Eve, and the parlour takes it all down
columns.body: Somebody let himself into the Hale house on 81st Street while the family was at Midnight Mass and left with the silver and a fur coat. He did not leave quietly. Mr. Hale has handed the police his parlour's record of the evening, and the police are listening very hard.

columns.headline: The ox comes through on two lines, and the hall picks up both
columns.body: After the eleven o'clock St. Rita's played the pageant record, and the ox came through in two places at once: the front at the manger, the back in the cloakroom, mooing on its own. Two hundred people laughed for a minute. Sister Bernadette says it was 'received well.'

columns.headline: Valve famine: the pawnbroker is the only man in Queens with good reception
columns.body: No valves at the Arcade, none in Jamaica, Flushing or Astoria. The Jackson Avenue pawnbroker has bought three hundred used ones at twelve cents. He sells them at a quarter. Ask him whose set they came out of. He will not hear you.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd has reached the Barrier and is looking for a door. We know the feeling.

record.ear: Fair and very cold. High 20. Low 9 tonight. Ice cutting to resume Saturday.

lead.headline: Parlour record names Christmas Eve burglar; former ice man held in Hale case
lead.deck: Detective Sergeant Moran plays 2 hours 10 minutes of the 81st Street record; a voice heard addressing the family's spaniel by name and giving its own; silver found at a Flushing pawnshop
lead.body: Detectives arrested Mr. Victor Lasko, 29, of Corona, at 5:20 p.m. yesterday in the Hale burglary of Christmas Eve. Detective Sergeant Edward Moran said the parlour record of Mr. Leonard Hale's house carries, at 12:14 a.m., a man's voice telling the family's spaniel, 'It's only Vic, Brownie, go back to sleep.' Mr. Lasko delivered the Hales' ice until October. The silver was recovered at a Flushing pawnshop. The fur coat has not been found. He is held in 2,500 dollars bail.

columns.headline: WORS 1610 carol: Phonautograph Society to send a record to Union Seminary
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens will send one of the two Woodside records of the carol heard on WORS 1610 on Christmas night to the hymnologist of the Union Theological Seminary, Mr. Cyril Abbot said yesterday. The second is to go into the 1978 case.

columns.headline: Interborough: 36 of 40 Astoria trains fitted with shoe heaters
columns.body: The Interborough reports 36 of its 40 Astoria line trains now fitted with contact shoe heaters, the remaining four promised by Monday. There was one delay from ice on the Queensboro Plaza curve on Christmas night, of six minutes.

columns.headline: Borough posts a second bill of 28 dollars to Signal Ground Rents Inc.
columns.body: Mr. Ludwig Haas of the Borough President's office posted a second bill to Signal Ground Rents Inc. yesterday, for 28 dollars, covering both thawings of the Vantry Arcade downpipe. The first bill of 14 dollars has been neither paid nor returned. The company's telephone was rung at 11 without reply.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd's ships turning east along the Barrier at 4 a.m. The Bay of Whales 'within a day.'

speaker.ear: Nine degrees tonight. High 20. The ice men are dusting off their saws.

lead.headline: Burglar says good night to the dog, and the parlour says hello to the police
lead.deck: 'It's only Vic, Brownie': twelve minutes past midnight, a spaniel, a former ice man and a room nobody thought was listening
lead.body: The Hales went to Midnight Mass. Vic Lasko went to the Hales'. At fourteen minutes past twelve the parlour heard him say, 'It's only Vic, Brownie, go back to sleep,' and Brownie did, and so, for two days, did the case. Then Sergeant Moran played the record. Mr. Lasko used to deliver the Hales' ice, which is how Brownie knew him and how the police found him. The silver was in Flushing. The fur coat is still out in the cold. Brownie is not being charged.

columns.headline: The mystery carol goes to the seminary to see if it rings a bell
columns.body: One record of Christmas night's WORS 1610 carol is going to the hymn man at Union Theological, who has heard everything sung in English since Wesley. The other goes in the box for 1978. Between them, somebody will know the tune. The Speaker would settle for the title.

columns.headline: Shoe heaters on 36 trains, and the Plaza curve warms to the idea
columns.body: Thirty-six of forty Astoria trains now have heated shoes, and the curve at the Plaza held them up just once on Christmas night, for six minutes. The last four trains by Monday. Then the elevated will be warmer underfoot than anyone who rides it.

columns.headline: Ground rent's bill goes to 28 dollars; the company keeps its receiver down
columns.body: The Borough has sent Signal Ground Rents Inc. a second bill, twenty-eight dollars, for two thawings of the Arcade downpipe. The first bill is still out there somewhere, unpaid and unreturned. The telephone at 120 Broadway rang at eleven yesterday. You know the rest. So does 120 Broadway.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Byrd is turning east along the Barrier, looking for the Bay of Whales. The whales are not answering either.

record.ear: Fair and cold. High 22. Low 10. Ice on the Sound eleven inches and making.

lead.headline: Mr. Pell asks the Senate committee to hear the Listening Act unrecorded
lead.deck: Landlords' counsel writes that a hearing on listening 'should not be prejudiced by being listened to'; committee room's system installed in 1911
lead.body: Mr. Lucius Pell, counsel to the Queens Real Estate Owners' Association, wrote to Senator Edmund Harlan yesterday asking that the Judiciary Committee's hearing of January 9 on the Listening Act be taken by stenographer only and the committee room's house system be disconnected for the day. The letter, of 212 words, states that a hearing on listening 'should not be prejudiced by being listened to.' The Senator's office said the room's system was installed in 1911 and 'nobody now present knows where it is switched.'

columns.headline: Ice cutting to resume on the Sound at 7 tomorrow; 210 men recalled
columns.body: The Bowery Bay Ice Company will recall its 210 laid-off men for 7 a.m. tomorrow, the Whitestone field having refrozen to eleven inches. Mr. Owen Pratt says the snow fence stays and the receiving set stays ashore. Cutting begins at the north end.

columns.headline: Mr. Lasko pleads not guilty; parlour record objected to by counsel
columns.body: Mr. Victor Lasko of Corona pleaded not guilty before Magistrate Doyle in Long Island City at 10 yesterday to burglary of the Hale house on Christmas Eve. His counsel objected to the parlour record as evidence. The Magistrate held him for the grand jury.

columns.headline: Phonautograph Society to station 40 recording parties for midnight Monday
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens will station 40 members with portable recorders from Long Island City to Far Rockaway to take down the borough at midnight on Monday for the 1978 case. Mr. Cyril Abbot asks the public to 'proceed as usual.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: The Record will play Commander Byrd's message from the Bay of Whales in its Jackson Avenue window as soon as received, day or night.

speaker.ear: Cold and clear. High 22. At the bottom of the world they call this a heat wave.

lead.headline: Byrd gets through to the Bay of Whales, and the whales take the call
lead.deck: The City of New York ties up to the ice at the bottom of the world; the Record plays his message in its window tonight, and we will be on the kerb with a thermos
lead.body: Commander Byrd's ships reached the Bay of Whales this morning by their own clock, which runs a day ahead of ours. He is at the Barrier, and the Barrier is the size of France and not interested. The message is on its way to Bay Shore. The Record will play it in its window on Jackson Avenue the minute it lands, and the Speaker will be outside in the snow, listening to the Record's window, which is how we get most of our news.

columns.headline: Landlords want the Listening Act heard with the switch off
columns.body: Mr. Lucius Pell has asked Albany to disconnect the committee room for the Listening Act hearing, so that listening is not listened to. The Senator's office says the room was wired in 1911 and nobody living knows where it turns off. Mr. Pell may bring a hammer.

columns.headline: Ice men back on the line at seven tomorrow
columns.body: Eleven inches on the Sound and making, and Bowery Bay wants its 210 men back at seven sharp tomorrow. The snow fence stays. The receiving set stays ashore. If WORS 1610 wants to be heard on the ice this winter, it will have to shout.

columns.headline: The Society will take Queens down at midnight Monday, and you are on the record
columns.body: Forty Phonautograph Society men with portable machines will stand at stations across the borough at midnight on New Year's Eve and record whatever Queens does. Mr. Abbot asks the public to 'proceed as usual.' The public will proceed as it usually does on New Year's Eve. Sorry, 1978.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Lasko's lawyer says the dog's evidence is hearsay. The dog has no comment.

record.ear: Snow flurries. High 25. Ice cutting resumed at Whitestone at 7.

lead.headline: Commander Byrd's message from the Bay of Whales played in the Record's window
lead.deck: Received at Bay Shore at 9:52 p.m. and wired to Jackson Avenue; heard by some 2,000 in light snow; played eleven times until 1:30 a.m.
lead.body: Commander Richard E. Byrd's first message from the Bay of Whales, received by the Navy at Bay Shore at 9:52 p.m., was played in the Record's window on Jackson Avenue at 10:14 last night to a crowd the police estimated at 2,000, standing in light snow. The message, of 61 words, reports the City of New York moored to the bay ice and 'all well; dogs well; base to be chosen tomorrow.' It was played eleven times until 1:30 a.m.

columns.headline: Week's count: 6,050 coal deliveries, 3,940 of them by horse
columns.body: The borough's coal dealers report 6,050 deliveries in the week to last night, 3,940 of them by horse, the motor trucks having stood idle on Christmas Eve for want of drivers. The Vernon Avenue yard reports that its Percheron Dutchman made 61 loads.

columns.headline: Interborough: 39 of 40 Astoria trains fitted; last on Monday
columns.body: The Interborough reports 39 of its 40 Astoria line trains fitted with contact shoe heaters, the fortieth to go into the Corona shop on Monday. There was no ice delay on the Queensboro Plaza curve in the week, the company reports.

columns.headline: Union Seminary hymnologist receives the WORS 1610 carol record
columns.body: Dr. Matthias Strand, hymnologist of the Union Theological Seminary, acknowledged yesterday the record of the carol heard on WORS 1610 on Christmas night. He told the Record he had played it three times 'and will play it again after the holiday.' He gave no opinion.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Joseph Marchetti has not been found. Justice Rourke sits on Mr. Pruitt's petition January 7.

speaker.ear: Flurries. High 25. Two thousand people stood in the snow last night to hear a man say he was cold.

lead.headline: Byrd calls home from the bottom of the world, and Jackson Avenue picks up
lead.deck: Two thousand in the snow outside the Record's window; eleven plays; one cheer per play, and a twelfth for the dogs
lead.body: At fourteen minutes past ten last night the Record's window on Jackson Avenue played Commander Byrd from the Bay of Whales, and two thousand people in the snow stopped breathing to hear it. Sixty-one words. 'All well; dogs well.' The crowd cheered the dogs louder than the Commander, which he would understand. The Record played it eleven times, until half past one. We stood through all eleven. By the eighth we could say it along with him. By the tenth so could the policeman.

columns.headline: Horses outpull the trucks in Christmas coal, and Dutchman carries the load
columns.body: Six thousand coal deliveries this week, nearly four thousand of them by horse, because the trucks had no drivers on Christmas Eve and the horses never ask. Dutchman made sixty-one loads. The trucks made excuses. Mr. Keller is thinking of selling a truck and buying a horse.

columns.headline: The seminary's hymn man plays the carol three times and holds the line
columns.body: Dr. Strand at Union Theological has the record of the WORS 1610 carol, has played it three times, and will not say what it is. A man who knows every hymn since Wesley does not know this one. Or he does, and is keeping us on hold.

columns.headline: Thirty-nine trains in warm shoes; the last one gets switched over Monday
columns.body: The Interborough has shoe heaters on thirty-nine of forty Astoria trains, and not one ice delay at the Plaza all week. The fortieth train goes into the shop on Monday. Guards say the third rail now sounds like bacon. We have stopped riding hungry.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Marchetti is still missing. The judge sits again January 7. The ledger is keeping its own counsel.

editorial.headline: The year's ten villains, and she is all of them
editorial.body: As is our custom, the Speaker names the year's villains. First, the woman called Lilith, for indecency. Second, Lilith, for trespass. Third, Lilith, for impersonating a corsage. We could go on to ten, and our stenographer, Miss Penrose, suggests we have. A word on circulation: the Speaker has sold thirty thousand more copies since November than in any season of its history, and our news agents report that the buyers are chiefly women, who buy two, one for themselves and one to leave on the trolley seat. We do not believe this is because of Lilith. We believe the women of Queens have at last discovered the Speaker's crossword. Happy New Year. Lock the safe.

record.ear: Fair and cold. High 26. Low 14. Ice at Whitestone twelve inches.

lead.headline: Elevated to run all night on New Year's Eve; 600 police to three centres
lead.deck: Trains every eight minutes until 4 a.m.; the Record's window to carry Times Square by wire from 11:30 p.m.; Phonautograph Society's 40 parties at their stations by 11
lead.body: The Interborough will run Astoria and Flushing line trains every eight minutes through the night of Monday until 4 a.m. Tuesday. Police Inspector Arthur Kane has ordered 600 men to Jamaica Avenue, Queens Plaza and Main Street, Flushing. The Record will carry the Times Square crowd by wire to its Jackson Avenue window from 11:30 p.m. The Phonautograph Society's 40 recording parties will be at their stations by 11. The Health Department reminds the public that celebratory gunfire is unlawful and 'audible in evidence.'

columns.headline: Party Line, the exchange cat, receives a parcel postmarked Corona
columns.body: A parcel addressed 'Party Line, Queens Exchange, Position 43' and containing a tin of sardines was delivered on Friday, the supervisor reports. It carried no sender's name and was postmarked Corona, December 27. The operators opened it in her presence.

columns.headline: Byrd chooses a base on the Barrier and names it Little America
columns.body: Commander Byrd's second message, received at Bay Shore at 3:10 a.m. yesterday, reports a site for the expedition's base chosen on the Barrier some miles from the ships, and unloading begun by dog team. The base is to be called Little America.

columns.headline: Used valves 35 cents on Jackson Avenue; Newark reopens Wednesday
columns.body: Used receiving valves were offered at 35 cents apiece on Jackson Avenue yesterday against 25 on Wednesday. The Newark works reopens on the 2nd. The Arcade hardware counter expects 400 sleeves by the 3rd and asks customers meanwhile to 'listen sparingly.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Ice cutting resumes Monday on the Willets Point field. Bowery Bay reports 1,400 tons cut yesterday.

speaker.ear: Fair and cold. High 26. Last Sunday of the year; do something you would like recorded.

lead.headline: Party Line gets fan mail: sardines from Corona, no return address
lead.deck: A tin arrives at the exchange for position 43; the operators open it in her presence; she says nothing, which is what an operator says
lead.body: Somebody in Corona sent the exchange cat a Christmas present. The parcel came Friday, addressed in a careful hand to 'Party Line, Queens Exchange, Position 43,' and inside was a tin of sardines. No card. No sender. The forty operators opened it in front of her, as is proper, and Party Line ate three sardines and went to sleep on the warm end of the board. We have asked around Corona. Nobody in Corona sent a cat sardines. Corona is very sure.

columns.headline: Byrd names his town Little America, and the penguins ask for an exchange
columns.body: Commander Byrd has picked a spot on the Barrier a few miles from the ships and named it Little America, which makes it the smallest and coldest suburb in the country. The dogs are hauling the furniture. There is no operator yet. They will want one.

columns.headline: New Year's Eve: the elevated stays up late and the police turn up the volume
columns.body: Trains every eight minutes until four on Tuesday morning, six hundred policemen on Jamaica Avenue and the Plaza, and the Record's window carrying Times Square by wire. The Health Department says shooting into the air is unlawful and, in Queens, recorded. Aim for the morning instead.

columns.headline: Second-hand valves hit thirty-five cents, and the pawnbroker turns up the gain
columns.body: A used valve that went for a quarter on Wednesday went for thirty-five cents on Jackson Avenue yesterday. Newark opens again on Wednesday. The Arcade counterman asks the borough to 'listen sparingly' until then, which is good advice for the whole year.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The ice men are back on the Willets Point field tomorrow. Fourteen hundred tons yesterday. Happy New Year, Sound.

record.ear: Fair and cold. High 28. Low 17 at midnight. Clear for the New Year.

lead.headline: Astoria Hum petition files 2,140 names; utility answers in one page
lead.deck: Queens Light & Power denies 'any tone at any frequency attributable to the company's works'; half-cent rise remains suspended to the January 15 hearing
lead.body: Alderman Feeney filed with the Public Service Commission on Saturday a list of 2,140 Astoria and Long Island City householders supporting the petition on the Hum, together with the cellar record of 1913 lent by Mr. Hesse of Ditmars Avenue. Queens Light & Power filed its answer the same afternoon. It runs to one page and denies 'any tone at any frequency attributable to the company's works.' The half-cent rise remains suspended. The Commission sits on both at 10 a.m. on January 15.

columns.headline: Athletic Club five beat the Jersey City Hibernians 35 to 22
columns.body: The Long Island City Athletic Club five beat the Jersey City Hibernians 35 to 22 at the armory on Saturday night before 1,300, Mr. Frank Dillon scoring 17. The club stands at five wins and four losses at the turn of the year.

columns.headline: Last Astoria train fitted with shoe heaters; Interborough reports work complete
columns.body: The Interborough fitted the fortieth and last of its Astoria line trains with contact shoe heaters at its Corona shop yesterday, completing the work by the date given on December 18. The company reports no ice delay at the Queensboro Plaza curve since Christmas night.

columns.headline: Record's window to carry Times Square by wire from 11:30 tonight
columns.body: The Record will carry the Times Square crowd by wire to its Jackson Avenue window from 11:30 tonight until 12:30, followed by Commander Byrd's message from the Bay of Whales, played once more at the public's request. The Phonautograph Society's 40 parties will record the borough at midnight.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Signal Ground Rents Inc. ends the year owing the Borough 28 dollars. Neither bill has been answered.

speaker.ear: Clear and cold for the New Year. High 28. Wrap up, ring out.

lead.headline: Ring out the old: Queens signs off on 1928 with the volume up
lead.deck: Trains till four, six hundred police, Times Square down the wire to Jackson Avenue, and forty men from the Society recording the lot for 1978
lead.body: Tonight the year ends, and Queens intends to be heard doing it. The Record's window will carry Times Square down the wire from half past eleven, and then Byrd one more time, because the crowd asked. The elevated runs until four. Six hundred policemen will stand about looking stern. Forty Phonautograph men will record the borough at midnight for 1978, so that 1978 knows what we sounded like happy. Kiss someone you mean. The walls are listening, and they are sentimental.

columns.headline: The Listening Lady: what 1928 said behind closed doors
columns.body: A count, a lineman, a postcard, a cat, a horse with a long memory, three dolls with too much to say, a carol nobody knows and a hum nobody makes. The Listening Lady heard it all, darlings, and repeats none of it, except in this column, nightly, for a penny.

columns.headline: Hum petition signs up 2,140 voices; the utility answers in one tone
columns.body: Alderman Feeney has filed 2,140 names and the baker's 1913 cellar with the Commission. Queens Light & Power has filed one page denying any tone at any frequency. The half cent stays suspended. January 15 at ten. Bring earplugs or bring a petition, but bring something.

columns.headline: Club five shoots Jersey City off the air, 35 to 22
columns.body: The Athletic Club five finished the year by beating the Jersey City Hibernians 35 to 22 at the armory, and Frank Dillon scored seventeen. Five won, four lost. Thirteen hundred hoarse men went home to tell their wives, who had heard it already through the wall.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Happy New Year from the Speaker. Marchetti, the ground rent and WORS 1610: still no answer from any of you.
